Battery optimisation, the Restricted choice, the permission reset and Battery Saver are all read from Android itself, so their states above are real. Restricted stops every background run outright; the permission reset takes the photos permission away from an app that is not opened for a few months, which is exactly what a set-and-forget app is; Battery Saver pauses runs until it is turned off, which most phones do by themselves while charging. Ente and Ente Photos belong to their owner and are named here only to say which app Ente Saver works with. Ente Saver is independent, and is not made by or connected with Ente.

Every official build is published at github.com/smmpanelusertestai07-dotcom/EnteSaver, with its checksum. Something wrong? Report it there; the page opens in your browser, Ente Saver itself never goes online.
What the app stores, and what it never does.

Ente Photos keeps your photos private with end-to-end encryption, and it stores exactly what you hand it — it does not make a file smaller first. So a library of 4K video fills a plan quickly, and the only answer usually on offer is to buy more storage every year.

Ente Saver is the step in between. It optimises your photos and videos on the phone itself, at the quality each one needs, so the same library takes a fraction of the space on the phone and in Ente — the free 10 GB or a small plan goes a great deal further.

It looks after the phone as well as the plan: it saves the heavy work for when the phone is charging, cool and idle, keeps the free space you asked it to keep, and finds duplicate files and your largest ones. An original goes only the way you chose: replaced and kept in the trash for 30 days, or freed by you.
Works entirely on your phone. No account, no ads, and no internet permission at all.

resources.string: It makes each photo and video in the albums you chose smaller, at the quality that file needs, on the phone. You choose how in Settings \u203a Saving space. Replace on this phone, the default, puts the smaller version in the original\u2019s place, with the same name, album and date, and keeps the original in the phone\u2019s trash for 30 days. If Ente Photos backs up that album, it uploads the smaller version in place of the one it holds, so your Ente storage shrinks too and no duplicate is made. Copies for Ente puts smaller copies in one folder for Ente Photos to back up, and leaves your originals as they are until you free them. Either way everything happens on the phone: Ente Saver has no internet permission and cannot upload anything itself.
Where do the smaller versions go, and what do I select in Ente Photos?

With Replace on this phone, nowhere new: each smaller version is in the original\u2019s own album, so in Ente Photos you back up those albums themselves \u2014 Settings \u203a Backup \u203a Backed up folders, with Camera and any other album you chose turned on. With Copies for Ente they go to Ente Saver\u2019s upload folder, Pictures/EnteSaver. In Settings you can give it your own name, or use separate folders for photos and videos, and the Storage screen prints the exact path with a copy button. In Ente Photos turn that folder on in Backed up folders, and turn off Camera, or you will be uploading the big originals as well. The folder also appears as an album in your gallery while files wait to be collected \u2014 that is what lets Ente see it. Anything you put into the folder yourself is left exactly where it is \u2014 Ente Saver never moves, renames or removes a file it did not create \u2014 but Ente Photos will upload it at full size, so Home shows a note whenever that happens.

Only if you choose Replace on this phone, and then safely. Before a file is replaced, a copy of the original is put in the phone\u2019s trash and checked byte for byte; only then is the smaller version written, and it is checked too. The original stays in the trash for 30 days, and Files \u203a the file \u203a Put the original back returns it to the same file. On Android 9 and 10, which have no trash, it waits as a hidden file beside the photo for the same 30 days. Home shows how much space the kept originals hold, with Delete them now if you want it back sooner. With Copies for Ente, originals are never edited, moved or deleted by the app: one is removed only if you open Free up space, select files yourself, and confirm Android\'s own deletion dialog. On Android 11 and newer it goes to your gallery trash first, where it stays about 30 days; on Android 10 Android removes it straight away and says so in its own dialog. Android 9 has no such dialog: there it is removed straight away once you confirm in Ente Saver.

Videos come out about seven times smaller, so a phone\u2019s videos fit Ente\u2019s free 10 GB for far longer. That size costs some detail. Tested on a phone screen, still scenes, screen recordings and most downloads look good; camera videos come out a little soft, and night scenes and games lose the most. On a large screen, side by side, the difference is plain. Photos keep what Google Photos\u2019 Storage saver keeps: above 16 megapixels they come down to 16. Videos come down to 1080p at up to 30 frames a second, while slow-motion clips keep their frame rate. A video Telegram, YouTube or WhatsApp already made smaller still comes down by two fifths at least. Files already as small as the app would make them, and anything a smaller version would damage, are left exactly as they are. With Replace on this phone the original waits 30 days, and Files can put it back.
Are dates, locations and file names kept?

Yes. A smaller version keeps the original\u2019s shooting date, camera details and format, and its location too, as long as you allowed the location request during setup \u2014 Android hands apps a copy with the location removed unless that one is granted. With Replace on this phone the file also keeps its name, album and date in the gallery, so nothing moves in your timeline or in Ente. With Copies for Ente the copy\u2019s name is the original\u2019s with a short code added, so it can always be matched back to its original, and its file date is set to match.
How does Ente Saver know a file reached Ente?

With Replace on this phone there is nothing to prove: the smaller version is the original\u2019s own file, and Ente Photos backs it up as it backs up that album. With Copies for Ente, two ways, both watched automatically. When you free up Ente Saver\u2019s folder in Ente (Albums \u203a Device \u203a Ente Saver\u2019s folder \u203a \u22ee \u203a Free up space), Ente removes the copies it has already uploaded from the folder; a copy that disappears without Ente Saver removing it is the proof. Ente Saver also adds copies a few at a time, and with Usage access on it watches how much data Ente Photos sends, so a matching amount right after one file goes out counts for that file. That weaker proof is used in Free up space only if you turn it on in Settings. Files with no proof are never offered for removal, and even with proof an original is offered only after a 30-day safety wait. Ente Photos has no daily data limit of its own, so Ente Saver\u2019s daily limit decides how much reaches Ente each day \u2014 added to the folder, or replaced on the phone. When Ente uploads, and on which network, is set inside Ente Photos.
How do I make Ente work like my phone\'s gallery?

Set Ente as the default gallery in Android Settings \u203a Apps \u203a Default apps, so most photos you open from other apps open in Ente. Give it a gallery-style icon, either with Ente\'s own setting (Ente \u203a Settings \u203a Appearance \u203a App icon) or with Ente Saver\'s icon pack in a launcher that supports icon packs. Or, from Help \u203a Make Ente your gallery, add a Photos shortcut to your home screen that opens Ente. Then turn on machine learning in Ente for face recognition and magic search. That help page walks through each step.
Someone deleted a file from the Ente Saver folder \u2014 what now?

If Ente Saver had already confirmed that file reached Ente, nothing happens: the disappearance is exactly what Free up device space in Ente Photos does, and the original was never at risk. If it had not been confirmed, Ente Saver treats the copy as lost and simply makes it again on the next run. Either way your original is untouched, because the app only ever removes an original after you confirm it yourself.
What about HEIC, RAW, GIF and motion photos?

Every file keeps its own format: a JPEG stays JPEG, a HEIC photo stays HEIC, and WebP and PNG stay WebP and PNG. A HEIC photo is made smaller only where this phone\u2019s chip can write HEIC, which a quick check finds out; elsewhere it is kept as it is. RAW, GIF and similar formats are kept exactly as they are, because optimising them either loses something that matters or makes the file bigger. Motion photos and depth photos are kept whole, so their moving or depth part stays intact, and Ultra HDR photos keep their HDR on Android 14 and newer. Anything kept unchanged is listed on the Files screen with the reason, so you can see it happened on purpose \u2014 it is the app refusing to damage something, not a failure.
What happens if I uninstall, clear data, or change phones?

Your photos are unaffected. Files replaced on this phone are your files, and their kept originals stay in the trash for the rest of their 30 days. Optimised copies stay in the Ente Saver folder until Ente Photos collects them, kept light copies stay in your gallery, and your Ente account is untouched. When you uninstall, Android asks whether to keep the app\'s data: keep it, and a reinstall carries on as before. Otherwise Ente Saver\'s history is saved every day as history.json in Documents \u203a Ente Saver. After a reinstall, or on a new phone with that file copied across, tap Restore from a saved file on the first screen and choose it, so nothing is optimised or sent twice. A file already made smaller is never made smaller again either way: it carries a note saying so.
What does freeing up space do, and can I get files back?

It is the one screen that can remove an original, and it only ever removes what you select. It lists files whose copies Ente has provably collected, shows the proof for each one, and offers three modes \u2014 keep a light copy in your gallery, remove the original entirely, or just clear the copies waiting on your phone. Unless you pick Delete permanently, removed files go to your gallery trash, where Android keeps them for 30 days, and the Recently freed up screen lists every batch with a Restore button. Delete permanently skips the trash and cannot be undone. Android 9 and 10 have no gallery trash, so there every removal is final; Android 10 also asks about each file on its own. If you choose the light-copy mode, the copies live in the Pictures/Light copies album \u2014 keep that album out of Ente\'s backed up folders, because every file there already reached Ente once and backing the album up would store it twice.

Nothing, from Ente Saver. The internet permission is removed from the app itself, so there is no code path that could send anything anywhere \u2014 not analytics, not crash reports, not your photos. All the network traffic you will see is Ente Photos uploading the folder, end-to-end encrypted, exactly as it would for any other folder. You can check what Ente Saver holds in Settings \u203a Permissions and battery \u203a What Ente Saver holds; network access is not on that list, because the app does not have it.
Why is there an Optimise now button if everything is automatic?

The schedule waits for good moments \u2014 charging, screen off, the day\u2019s allowance. The button skips the waiting, never the safety limits: it will not run when the phone is too hot, the battery is under 15%, or free space is below the reserve. The run is listed in Activity as \u201cStarted by you\u201d.
What is the Documents \u203a Ente Saver folder?

It holds one small text file, history.json: a list of file names, dates, sizes and short codes \u2014 never photos. It is rewritten every day, and it is what lets a reinstall or a new phone pick up where you left off: tap Restore from a saved file on the first screen and choose it. Deleting it is safe; the app writes it again within a day. Older versions kept this list in folders called .cloudsaver or _.cloudsaver; any left over can be deleted. Save and restore settings, under Settings \u203a Show advanced settings, makes an extra copy you keep somewhere else, like a computer.
Where do the “Recommended for this phone” figures come from?

From this phone, measured on the spot: how much storage it has in total, and how much of it is free right now. A 64 GB phone and a 512 GB phone should not hold back the same headroom. So Ente Saver keeps about a twentieth of the phone free (at least 1.5 GB), lowers its daily limit on a small or nearly full phone, and uses at most a tenth of the free space for its own work, up to 5 GB. Nothing is measured off the phone and no usage is sent anywhere. It is only ever an offer: the figure sits under the setting with a Use recommended button, your own value is never overwritten, and the line turns into a warning only when what is stored has drifted more than three times away from it.
Can the smaller version stay in the same album instead of a new folder?

Yes \u2014 that is Replace on this phone, the default, in Settings \u203a Saving space. Each smaller version is written into the original\u2019s own file: the same name, album and date, and the same format, so your gallery timeline does not move and no extra folder appears. If Ente Photos backs up that album, it uploads the smaller version in place of the one it holds, and no duplicate is made. Ente takes a few files at a time, so after a big batch its storage figure falls over a day or so. Android asks once for All files access, which is what lets Ente Saver write into photos other apps made, and it needs Location inside photos, so every file keeps where it was taken. A photo or video changed in the last hour waits for a later run, so a camera still finishing it, or Ente still uploading it, never meets a file being rewritten. The original waits in the phone\u2019s trash for 30 days, and Files can put it back. Ente Saver recognises a file it made smaller, so it is never optimised a second time.
Why only Ente Photos, and what if it isn\'t installed?

Ente Photos is end-to-end encrypted and keeps every file exactly as it was sent, so the space Ente Saver saved is the space you keep. When it frees up device space it removes its own uploads from the folder, which is how Ente Saver proves a copy arrived. It checks duplicates by content, so a file sent twice is stored once. And if Ente downloads a copy back to your phone \u2014 into Download or any album \u2014 Ente Saver recognises its own copies by their names and never optimises or re-sends them. You also get one recovery key and one timeline, with Ente\'s on-device face recognition and magic search. If Ente Photos is not installed yet, copies are still made and wait in the folder, using the space you allowed. Nothing is ever freed until Ente has them. Install it from the Play Store, F-Droid or ente.com, turn on the Ente Saver folder in it, and the waiting copies go up on its next backup.
Why does the Files list look empty when Free up space still finds things?

They answer different questions. Files is the work list: it shows what Ente Saver is going to optimise and what it already has, so it only ever covers the albums you ticked. Free up space is a cleaning tool for the phone as a whole \u2014 duplicates and your largest files are found in every album, ticked or not, because a duplicate wastes space wherever it sits. If Files looks empty, the usual reason is that no album is ticked yet; the list says so, and Settings has the album picker.
Why is nothing happening, or why did it stop?

Ente Saver works in the background and waits for good moments on purpose, so a quiet hour is normal. When it waits longer, one of these is the reason, and Home says which. Battery Saver pauses it until Battery Saver is off (most phones switch it off while charging); Super power saving or Ultra battery saver stops every background app while it is on. Charging-only mode waits for the charger. On Realme, Oppo, Xiaomi and Vivo phones, auto-launch switched off is the usual reason it stops a day after setup \u2014 Settings \u203a Permissions and battery opens that page, with the path to it. Android also runs an app less often when it is rarely opened; opening Ente Saver now and then helps. Optimise now on Home runs it straight away, within the safety limits.
How do I know this copy of Ente Saver is the real one?

Every official build is published at github.com/smmpanelusertestai07-dotcom/EnteSaver, and each release prints two long codes: one for the file itself and one for the key it was signed with. The file\u2019s code changes with every build; the key\u2019s code is the same for every genuine Ente Saver there will ever be. Android checks that key for you: a build signed with a different one cannot install over this app at all. Installed on its own, after this one is removed, it would open and say so on Home, and it would keep deletion switched off. Installing from a file rather than a store is also why the phone shows a Play Protect warning the first time: \u201cMore details\u201d, then \u201cInstall anyway\u201d.
